issues.description: PR scope creep: test additions hidden under README reformat and FAQ entry
issues.detail: Stated goal is POST tests for things_advanced, but the diff also rewrites the README example (style, handle() signature, status formatting, str.format) and adds an FAQ. Three patches in one. Split it so the test change can be reviewed cleanly and the reformat lands with its own justification.

issues.description: Silent swap from req.stream to req.bounded_stream changes contract without justification
issues.detail: things_advanced.py changes body = req.stream.read() to req.bounded_stream.read(). These have different preconditions under WSGI: bounded_stream enforces Content-Length, stream does not. The PR description and diff disagree, and no docstring, versionchanged, or comment explains why. Code was bent to make the new test pass.

issues.description: README handle() signature reorder is an undocumented drive-by change
issues.detail: The README snippet reorders StorageError.handle from (ex, req, resp, params) to (req, resp, ex, params). Whether or not this matches modern Falcon, the commit message says nothing about it, and readers copying the old vs new form hit a substitution failure against the framework's expected callable. Justify in the commit or drop.

issues.description: FAQ example handler has nested control flow and unbounded read
issues.detail: PostTest.on_post nests if/else where three flat branches read better, and calls req.stream.read(req.content_length or 0) with a client-supplied length — a copy-paste footgun for unbounded allocation. Example code in user docs is imitated; write the flat form and use bounded_stream or state the bound.

issues.description: FAQ test uses parenthesized assert — Python footgun
issues.detail: assert(result.status == ...) reads like a function call and trains readers toward the broken assert(x, y) tuple form that always passes. In canonical example code that teaches testing, write assert result.status == falcon.HTTP_400.

issues.description: New POST tests assert status codes without naming the contract under test
issues.detail: resp3 and resp4 check status codes but no comment or docstring states which invariant of things_advanced is being verified (auth + JSON + body-required). A future maintainer reading a failure cannot tell whether the 400 is spec or accident. Add a one-line spec comment per assertion block.

synthesis.summary: The panel agrees the test additions themselves are useful but the PR is undisciplined: it bundles three changes (POST tests, a README reformat with a handle() signature reorder, and a new FAQ entry) under a title that promises only the first. The decisive technical concern is the silent swap from req.stream to req.bounded_stream in things_advanced.py — a contract change that was made to bend the example to fit the new test rather than reasoned from spec. The FAQ example has additional taste issues (nested control flow, parenthesized assert, unbounded client-supplied read) that matter because docs code is copied. Recommendation: split the PR, document the contract change, and clean up the FAQ snippet before merge.
